Cemetery services
Cemetery services
Seven of Metro’s historic cemeteries are open for new burials. Contact our staff to learn how to purchase space for a casket or cremation urn, as well as other cemetery services. 
Lone Fir Cemetery
Metro manages 14 historic cemeteries around Multnomah County, from scenic Corbett to the top of Sylvan Hill in southwest Portland. Seven of these cemeteries are open for new sales. Whether you’re interested in purchasing a burial space, locating an old family burial plot, or replacing the marker at an existing grave, the first step is to contact Metro’s cemetery staff by phone or email. 
Why choose a Metro cemetery?
People have many reasons for choosing one of Metro’s cemeteries as the final resting place for themselves or their loved ones. Some are attracted to the cemeteries’ rich histories and their beautiful natural settings. Others want to be laid to rest near family who are already buried at a cemetery. 
Many people also appreciate that because Metro is a government agency, it has a commitment to keeping its fee rates as affordable as possible. Metro’s caring and professional cemetery staff do not work on commission and have experience with diverse burial customs.  
Whether you are making arrangements for a recently deceased loved one or pre-planning for the future, Metro staff can help explain your options and guide you through the process. They can also help you locate applications for specialized services like those available to U.S. military veterans and their families.
How to purchase cemetery services
Whatever service you are interested in purchasing, the first step is to contact Metro cemetery staff by phone at 503-797-1709 or by email at Metro.Cemeteries@oregonmetro.gov . Metro cemetery staff work remotely and are not available for in-person office visits. Information to leave in your message includes: 
Your name and contact information 
The services and cemetery you are interested in 
Any needs you have for language interpretation and/or disability accommodations 
A Metro staff member will return your call or email during normal weekday working hours. They will guide you through possible options and costs. 
Available services
Burials
Fees for burials and related services vary depending on the cemetery and the type of preferred burial, casket or cremation urn. Metro’s cemeteries price list describes options and current charges.

Cremation
There are several options for cremated urn placements in Metro cemeteries. Along with in-ground burials, Metro offers placement in a columbarium at Chestnut Grove Memorial Garden in Lone Fir cemetery.

Cemeteries open to new sales
Cemetery
Columbia Pioneer Cemetery
At nearly 2.5 acres, Columbia Pioneer Cemetery is a green oasis at busy Northeast Sandy Boulevard and 99th Avenue in Portland’s Parkrose neighborhood. While cars pass by, inside it’s a peaceful neighborhood green space enjoyed by many.
Cemetery
Douglass Cemetery
Amidst wide swaths of lawn, a grove of Douglas firs offers a woodland feel and a beautiful place for reflection. At 9.1 acres of lawn and forest, Douglass is one of Metro’s larger cemeteries.
Cemetery
Jones Cemetery
Hidden in Portland’s Sylvan neighborhood, this 3.5-acre green jewel perches high on a south-facing hill, with open lawns and views across the Tualatin Valley to the Chehalem Mountains.
Cemetery
Lone Fir Cemetery
Nestled in Southeast Portland, Lone Fir Cemetery is more than just a cemetery. It’s also one of Oregon’s most treasured historic places and Portland’s second-largest arboretum.
Cemetery
Mountain View Corbett Cemetery
With stunning views of Mount Hood and the Washington Cascades, this rural two-acre cemetery occupies a small grassy rise surrounded by vegetable farms, vineyards and orchards in Corbett.
Cemetery
Pleasant Home Cemetery
Located at Bluff and Pleasant Home roads in Gresham, burial plots are on the north end of the cemetery; the south end slopes to beautiful forest along Johnson Creek.
Cemetery
Powell Grove Cemetery
Located at Northeast 122nd Avenue at Sandy Boulevard, an early market road to Portland, the cemetery is the final resting place for members of the Powell and Reynolds families, early settlers of what is now Portland’s Parkrose neighborhood.
